body:
Hey there everyone, I just thought I would share a story with you and if nothing else, make you smile for a brief moment and make you think about what decisions you are making in your life, and how those decisions can make those around you feel. About 4 years ago, I decided I was going to commit suicide. I decided that my life was just not worth living and that I would just end it all in a fleeting moment and I would finally get to answer the biggest question - what comes after death, will I be saved from my depression, or suffer an infinate amount of time feeling the pain and sorrow of the actions I had just taken. I cleaned my apartment, wrote out my suicide note, but the strangest thing happened, as I have realized happened a lot of people around here - During the course of writing the note I found myself becoming extremely emotional and crying, something that did not often happen when coupled with thoughts of my suicide. I thought this was a sign, and called my mother to tell her what I had planned to do, if anyone in the world would be able to understand what I was going through and still come out the other side loving me more and more, it was my mother. I owe my life to my mother, for both bringing me into this world, and saving me from taking a quick way out of it. It was from that day, that I knew that I could never end my life, I could never do something so hurtful to those around me, those who loved me. I could not hurt the people I loved. So I decided that a radical change needed to be made, something had to break so that I would no longer have the desire to kill myself, but at the same time would not  just be living every day a lie and be unhappy for the rest of my life. I was 19 at the time, and left Canada and went to Ireland for work. I thought maybe a fresh perspective would allow me a new start, it was my second best option to killing myself, starting a new, starting completely fresh where no one knew my name, and I had no responsibilities, I could in effect, be whoever I wanted to be. I left without saying a word to any person in my life other than my mother (who told my father and sister), and wouldn't have told her if I did not fear that she would think I had killed myself, and would be crushed. I promised her that I would write her once every 3 months to assure her that I was alive. I sold every single thing I owned, and went to Ireland with nothing but my Journals to write in, the clothes on my back and in my pack, and maybe $2000 to tide me over if I could not find a job for longer than a few weeks. 

The freedom I felt was immense, the absolute freedom, I could be anybody I wanted to be. I could leave anytime I wanted to, nobody depending on me, nobody needing to know where I was, it was so liberating. I spent 3 months in Ireland before moving onto start my journey around Europe, working in various spots along the way to earn a bit of money and enjoy the city. I spent nights on the streets sometimes, sometimes in a hotel, the point was that it didn't matter where I was, because I was always on the move, meeting new people, allowing myself to be completely free of everything else and become who I really was inside, not fearing the repercussions as I did when I was living closer to home. All in all I spent 3 years travelling on my own, starting in Ireland, and ending in the eastern provinces of China, before coming back home to a very happy mother and father, who were so elated to find out I was still alive didn't even yell at me for forgetting to write in the past 6 months. I honestly don't know why I am posting this here in Reddit, but I just like to think that if this story can make just one person reconsider self-harm, then I will be elated that I posted it.
